glossary.definition: A multimodal AI system can work with more than one type of input or output, understanding both text and images, for example, or generating text plus audio, instead of being limited to just one format. Show it a photo of your fridge and ask "what can I cook with this," and a multimodal model can actually look at the picture and reason about the ingredients, the way a person glances at the fridge and starts planning dinner, rather than needing everything typed out in words first.

items.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
items.summary: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies. Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday , up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies. The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.

items.title: Optimizely confirms massive cyberattack on customer websites injected stealer malware
items.summary: Attackers apparently from China used an authentication security hole within the popular Optimizely AI platform for marketers to steal from at least 178 sites owned by some of the planet’s largest companies. Named victims featured vendors including Zoom, Paychex, Equifax, and GitLab, and end-user enterprises including Starbucks, IKEA, Mattel, American Eagle, Air France, Mutual of Omaha, Heineken, Home Chef, Cinnabon, American Eagle, Levi, Costco and HSBC. Salesforce issued a statement confirming that it had also been impacted by the attack. “Salesforce is investigating unauthorized modifications to scripts provided by Optimizely and used on certain Salesforce websites,” it wrote in an email statement.

items.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
items.summary: " The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.summary: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop. Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang , the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop. On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance.

items.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
items.summary: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO. As Nvidia reported its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, the company’s financial performance was overshadowed by the drama surrounding its former CEO . And Nvidia’s board made one thing clear right off the bat: Jensen Huang isn’t coming back . At the start of the earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones emphasized the company’s strength and “groundbreaking technology” before turning to the circumstances surrounding Huang’s departure.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
items.summary: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, two new models that are more capable and cheaper than their predecessors. In the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Astra ranks second behind Claude Fable 5.2, and it is the first released model to reach the High threshold for AI self-improvement on OpenAI's own scale. OpenAI itself classifies that as a risk. OpenAI releases two new language models.

items.title: Inspiring FOSS project Crosspoint Reader has lessons about tech, communities, and LLMs
items.summary: The Ubuntu Summit isn't all about Ubuntu, or even Linux. The second day opened with a talk from CrossPoint Reader project lead Justin Mitchell, with both good and bad news for all kinds of FOSS. The talk, EPUBs, ESP32s, and Everyone's A Developer Now, was all about a FOSS project that isn't Linux-based – because the devices it targets are much too small to run even the smallest, most cut-down distro. Recently, a new generation of roughly credit-card sized ebook readers has been thriving.

items.title: HCLTech Partners With Transformer Co-Author-Led Cohere to Target Sovereign AI Markets
items.summary: HCLTech and Cohere have partnered to build and deliver sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) solutions for enterprises and governments. Under the agreement, HCLTech will become one of Cohere's preferred global systems integrator partners in Canada and Germany. The companies plan to combine Cohere's sovereign AI platform and models with HCLTech's professional services and AI implementation capabilities. They also intend to extend the partnership to other markets.

items.title: Microsoft’s outage should terrify every enterprise
items.summary: I’ve been in cloud computing long enough to see just about every kind of failure: bad deployments, network failures, identity outages, botched DNS changes, overloaded regions, misconfigured automation, and old-fashioned human error wrapped in a shiny cloud-native package. Most outages are expensive and annoying. Some are embarrassing. A few become case studies. The scale, duration, and downstream impact of what just happened are unlike anything I’ve seen in my career.
